Salé, the 'Republic of Salé' on the Bou Regreg

capitals.note: Coordinates approximate (taken at Taroudant, Souss valley); the page gives no site.

rulers.name: Ahmad al-Araj
rulers.note: The page gives no reign years: named successor in 1513, took Marrakesh 1524/25, exiled 1543; 1517 is al-Qa'im's death year.

rulers.name: Ahmad al-Mansur
rulers.note: Died of the plague on 25 August 1603.

rulers.name: Abu Faris (Marrakesh line)
rulers.note: The page says 'Marrakesh until 1606; assassinated 1609'; 1603 is al-Mansur's death year. The Fez line: Muhammad al-Ma'mun from 1604 (fled to Spain 1608, killed 1613), Abdallah al-Ghalib II at Fez 1609-1623, Abd al-Malik al-Mu'tasim after 1623 (d. 1627).

rulers.name: Ahmad al-Abbas
rulers.note: Assassinated in 1659 (1658 or 1659 on the page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Saadi row starts in 1556, but the infobox gives 'Established / disestablished: 1510 / 1659' and capitals 'Tidsi (1510-1513); Afughal (1513-1525); Marrakesh (1525-1659)'. The page gives no boundary for 1510-1523, so the Souss is the researcher's reading of the first capitals; Wattasid Fez and the Portuguese coast are outside it.

correction.text: the Saadi principality in the Souss around Tidsi and Afughal, before the capture of Marrakesh

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Marrakesh 'finally taken' by al-Araj in '1524 or 1525' and Morocco 'partitioned roughly along the Oum Er-Rbia River' by the 1527 Treaty of Tadla, so the Saadi realm 1524-1548 is the south of the Oum Er-Rbia. The Portuguese enclaves at Agadir (until 1541) and Safi and Azemmour (evacuated 1541) lie inside this region but were not Saadi until the dated events; other Portuguese coastal places also remain outside. The page gives no area.

correction.text: Marrakesh and the south of Morocco: the Saadi realm south of the Oum Er-Rbia, fixed by the 1527 Treaty of Tadla

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The siege lasted until January 28, 1549, when the Saadians finally took the city' (Fez), so the Saadi realm is all of Morocco from 1549, three years before Cliopatria's 1556 shape. Exceptions: the Ottoman-backed Abu Hassun held Fez in 1554 (January to September on the Saadi page's two dates), and Cliopatria's Portuguese Africa row (1507-1581) is a neighbour along the coast. Tlemcen was held June 1550 to February 1551 as an occupation (ledger).

correction.text: all of Morocco after the fall of Fez on 28 January 1549, as in Cliopatria's 1556 Saadi shape

keyframe_review.note: 384,418 km2: Morocco after the Wattasid fall. The Saadi page gives no area (infobox silent). The Portuguese and Spanish coastal places are Cliopatria neighbours (Portuguese Africa 1556-1581, Spanish Empire 1556-1669) and are carved out of the shape's coast. The Cliopatria 1556 shape runs to 1581 and the 1582 shape (Touat, Gourara, Taghaza) is used only from 1583, so 1582 itself is drawn as this shape (Morocco alone; the Pashalik page dates Touat and Gourara to 1583).

577,829 km2: Morocco plus the Sahara north-west of the Niger. The Pashalik page: Touat and Gourara occupied in 1583, the Taghaza salt mines 'in 1556-57 and again in 1586'. The shape is right for 1583-1590 but starts a year early; from 1591 the Niger bend is added (new keyframe saadi-sultanate_1591, which supersedes this shape for 1591-1594). The year 1582 therefore falls to the 1556 shape (saadi-sultanate_1556).

correction.text: the shape unchanged, holding 1583-1590: Morocco with the Touat and Gourara oases (1583) and Taghaza (1586); the year 1582 is drawn as the 1556 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Niger bend is Saadi land from 1591 ('Moroccan Governorate (1591-1621)'; Timbuktu captured 30 May 1591, Djenné 1592) to the end of direct control in 1618; Cliopatria's 1595 shape is used for 1591-1613, and from 1614 the same shape without the Souss (saadi-sultanate_1614). The Pashalik page gives no area. After 1612 the Arma governor ruled in practice (the same page), so 1612-1617 is a nominal hold.

correction.text: Morocco, the Touat and Gourara oases, Taghaza and the Pashalik of Timbuktu on the Niger

keyframe_review.note: 841,482 km2, the maximum: Morocco, the Sahara and the Niger bend. 'In October 1590, he dispatched a force under Judar Pasha'; the Niger was reached on 28 February 1591, Tondibi fell on 13 March 1591 and Timbuktu on 30 May 1591 (Pashalik page), so the shape is right in its extent but the Niger bend is Saadi from 1591, not 1595; the new keyframe saadi-sultanate_1591 holds it 1591-1617. The Tondibi page notes Morocco was 'unable to assert firm control over the area'.

577,829 km2 would have the Niger bend leave the realm in 1600. No page says so: the Pashalik page has Timbuktu a 'Moroccan Governorate (1591-1621)' and that Moulay Zidan 'relinquished direct control over the Sudan territories in 1618'. Use the 1595 shape until 1613 (new keyframe saadi-sultanate_1591) and without the Souss for 1614-1617 (saadi-sultanate_1614).

correction.text: the full 1595 shape (Morocco, Touat, Taghaza and the Niger bend), kept until 1613; from 1614 to 1617 the same shape without the Souss (saadi-sultanate_1614)

keyframe_review.note: 384,140 km2, Morocco alone, for 1609-1611 is too early: the Niger bend was still a governorate until direct control was given up in 1618. The Pashalik page adds that 'after 1612' the Arma commander deposed the governor and proclaimed himself pasha, so control was nominal from then; the map keeps the governorate colour to 1617 and the vassal tint after.

correction.text: the full 1595 shape, kept until 1613; from 1614 to 1617 without the Souss (saadi-sultanate_1614)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Souss leaves the realm in 1614. The Saadi page: 'The Sous valley, meanwhile, had come under the leadership of 'Ali Abu Hassun al-Simlali in the town of Iligh since 1614'; the Dila'iya page lists, after Moulay Zidan's accession in 1613, 'the Sus, until Draa River, under the control of the Zaouia of Illigh'. The Draa valley itself is taken in 1631 (ledger 1631), so it stays in this shape; the radius that separates the Draa valley from the Souss is the researcher's reading. The Niger bend is still held (nominally from 1612, vassal from 1618).

correction.text: the 1595 shape (Morocco, Touat, Taghaza, the Niger bend) without the Souss, which was 'under the control of the Zaouia of Illigh', 1614-1617

keyframe_review.note: 384,090 km2: right from 1618, when the Pashalik page says direct control over the Sudan was relinquished (the Niger bend then a nominal vassal, ledger 1618). For 1612-1617 the new keyframe saadi-sultanate_1591 overrides it. The realm was split between Marrakesh and Fez 1603-1627 (Saadi page) but both lines are Saadi, so one colour. Corrected in the repair pass: the Souss, which the Saadi page has under Ali Abu Hassun at Iligh 'since 1614', is removed from this shape (ledger 1614).

correction.text: Morocco without the Souss (Illigh since 1614), holding 1618-1628, with the Niger bend a nominal vassal

keyframe_review.note: 384,418 km2: the reunified realm after 1627 ('the two Saadian splinter states in Marrakesh and Fes were finally reunified'). Corrected in the repair pass: the Souss has been 'under the leadership of 'Ali Abu Hassun al-Simlali in the town of Iligh since 1614' (Saadi page; ledger 1614), and the Draa valley and the Tafilalt go in 1631 (ledger 1631, shape saadi-sultanate_1631), so this shape holds only for 1629-1630. The Dala'iyya, a Middle Atlas brotherhood, 'defeated a Saadian army in 1638' (Saadi page).

correction.text: the 1629 shape without the Souss, holding 1629-1630; from 1631 the Draa valley and the Tafilalt are also gone (saadi-sultanate_1631)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: in 1631 Ali Abu Hassun of Iligh 'went on to conquer the Dra'a Valley and then as far Sijilmasa in the Tafilalt' (Saadi page) and the Alawi page has 'Mawlay al-Sharif ... declared sultan of the Tafilalt in 1631' (Morocco founds the Alawi state at Sijilmasa the same year). The Saadi realm is the 1629 shape without the Souss-Draa (the Sous region of the gazetteer spans the Draa valley) and without the Tafilalt (80 km around Sijilmasa). The pages disagree on who held the Tafilalt in 1631-1640 (Abu Hassun on the Saadi page; the Alawite on the Alawi page); both are non-Saadi.

correction.text: the 1629 shape without the Souss and the Draa valley (Illigh) and without the Tafilalt around Sijilmasa (the Alawis), 1631-1639

keyframe_review.note: 384,641 km2 to 1669 is wrong for every year after 1640: the Dila'iya page says 'by 1641 they had taken Meknes, Fez, and Salé' and 'In Fez, the Saadi family was expelled', and the Saadi page ends the dynasty in 1659 with the assassination of Ahmad al-Abbas. The verdict is adjust for 1640 itself (the shape without the Souss-Draa and the Tafilalt, as saadi-sultanate_1631); for 1641-1659 use the Marrakesh core (new keyframe saadi-sultanate_1641); after 1659 there is no Saadi land (ledger 1659).

correction.text: the 1640 shape without the Souss-Draa and the Tafilalt, holding 1640 only; from 1641 the Dila'iya hold Fez, Meknes and Salé and the Saadi keep the Marrakesh rump (saadi-sultanate_1641)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Fez, Meknes and Salé went to the Dila'iya by 1641 the Saadi sultans kept Marrakesh until 1659 (infobox capital 1525-1659). The pages give no boundary of the rump, so Marrakesh and the Haouz are the researcher's reading; the page says the Souss to the Draa was under the Zawiya of Illigh. The land that leaves the 1640 shape is accounted for in the ledger of 1641: Fez, Meknes and Salé (confidence 3) and the rest of the Dila'iya domain (confidence 2) to the Dila'iya, and the remainder of the realm to nobody (confidence 1: no page names a holder).

652.8 km2 (bbox 29.60-29.92 N, 5.59-6.04 W, in the Draa valley) for 1670-1737 is unsupported: the Saadi page ends the dynasty in 1659 ('Ahmad al-Abbas was assassinated in 1659, bringing the dynasty to an end') and the Alawi page has the Alawi sultan holding Marrakesh from July 1668. No page places a Saadi holding in the Draa after 1659. The land is Alaouite Morocco's (Cliopatria 'Morocco' from 1670).

correction.text: no Saadi land after 1659; the Draa valley is part of Alaouite Morocco

keyframe_review.note: 652.8 km2 for 1738-1740, the same unsupported patch as 1670; the dynasty ended in 1659.

correction.text: no Saadi land after 1659; Alaouite Morocco

region.text: Tidsi, the first capital (1510-1513)

ledger.note: 1510: the Saadi sultanate is established at Tidsi. Infobox 'Established 1510'; capitals 'Tidsi (1510-1513); Afughal (1513-1525)'. The page names the capital, not the Souss; the region is the researcher's reading.
1513: the Saadi seat moves from Tidsi to Afughal (infobox 'Afughal (1513-1525)').

region.text: Marrakesh, whose Kasbah al-Araj captured 'thus finally taking control of the city'

ledger.note: 1524: Ahmad al-Araj takes Marrakesh. The page says 1524 or 1525 and that al-Araj 'had Bu Shantuf killed and captured the Kasbah'; the Wattasid page has 'seized Marrakesh in 1524'. The south is read from the 1527 partition along the Oum Er-Rbia.
1525: Marrakesh becomes the Saadi capital (infobox 'Marrakesh (1525-1659)').

region.text: Agadir, captured from the Portuguese

ledger.note: 1541: Muhammad al-Shaykh takes Agadir. 'In 1541 Muhammad al-Shaykh captured Agadir from the Portuguese.'

region.text: Safi and Azemmour, evacuated by the Portuguese that year

ledger.note: 1541: the Portuguese leave Safi and Azemmour. The page says they 'evacuate[d] Azemmour and Safi that same year'; it does not describe a Saadian capture, hence confidence 2.

region.text: Fez and the Wattasid north

ledger.note: 28 January 1549: the Saadians take Fez. 'The siege lasted until January 28, 1549, when the Saadians finally took the city.' The Wattasid page says 1550 for the conquest of Fez; the Saadi page's day is followed. The region (the whole north) is the researcher's reading.

region.text: 'the Portuguese evacuated Ksar al-Seghir and Asilah in 1550'

ledger.note: 1550: the Portuguese evacuate Ksar es-Seghir and Asilah. 'Further north, the Portuguese evacuated Ksar al-Seghir and Asilah in 1550' (Saadi page); the page does not say to whom, and the region (two coastal places) is the researcher's reading. The Asilah page has the Portuguese conquest in 1471 and 'abandoned because of an economic debt crisis in 1549', so the year is 1549 or 1550 and 1550 is followed here. The pages opened say nothing on who held Asilah between 1550 and 1589 (the reviewer's handover of 1577 is on no page opened), so the dossier carries it as Saadi land to 1589 (bridging). Neither place is inside Cliopatria's Saadi shapes, so the keyframes do not draw them.

region.text: Tlemcen, which the Saadians 'conquered ... in June 1550'

ledger.note: June 1550: the Saadians take Tlemcen. 'conquered the city in June 1550'; Ottoman forces expelled them in February 1551.

region.text: Tlemcen, from which 'Ottoman forces expelled them'

ledger.note: February 1551: Ottoman forces drive the Saadians out of Tlemcen.

region.text: Fez, lost to the Ottoman-backed Abu Hassun

ledger.note: January 1554: the Ottoman-backed Abu Hassun defeats the Saadians and holds Fez. The page says he 'defeated the Saadians in January 1554' and that Muhammad al-Shaykh 'retook Fez in September 1554'; the Wattasid page says he 'briefly retook Fez in 1554'.

region.text: Fez, retaken by Muhammad al-Shaykh

ledger.note: September 1554: Muhammad al-Shaykh retakes Fez; the Wattasid dynasty is finished (Battle of Tadla, undated on the page).

region.text: the Taghaza salt mines: 'In 1556-7 Sultan Muhammed al-Shaykh briefly occupied Taghaza and killed the Askia's representative'

ledger.note: 1556: Muhammad al-Shaykh occupies Taghaza. 'In 1556-7 Sultan Muhammed al-Shaykh briefly occupied Taghaza and killed the Askia's representative' (Taghaza page; the Pashalik page has the same '1556-57 and again in 1586'). The page gives a span, not a day; the start year 1556 and the end year 1557 are the two ends of that span. The land is drawn as occupation, not as part of the realm, because the occupation was brief.

region.text: Taghaza, 'briefly occupied'

ledger.note: 1557: the first Saadi occupation of Taghaza ends. The page says only that the occupation of '1556-7' was 'brief'; the end year is the page's span, the cause is not given. The Taghaza page has the Saadians occupy it 'again' in 1586 (ledger 1586).

region.text: the Touat and the Gourara oases, 'successfully occupied' by al-Mansur's forces in 1583

ledger.note: 1583: Ahmad al-Mansur's forces occupy the Touat and Gourara oases. 'In 1583 Al-Mansur's forces successfully occupied the Touat and the Gourara oases.' The oasis lords are not named; the coordinates are the researcher's.

region.text: the Taghaza salt mines, occupied by Saadi forces 'in 1556-57 and again in 1586'

ledger.note: 1586: Saadi forces occupy the Taghaza salt mines again. The Pashalik page gives '1556-57 and again in 1586'; the Tondibi page lists the mines among the Songhai places the Moroccans 'captured, plundered, and razed' (undated). Cliopatria's shape reaches 23.1 N from 1582. The owner of Taghaza is the researcher's reading (Songhai).

region.text: Asilah: 'in 1589 the Saadians briefly regained control of Asilah, but then lost it to the Spanish'

ledger.note: 1589: Asilah goes to Spain. The Asilah page: 'in 1589 the Saadians briefly regained control of Asilah, but then lost it to the Spanish'; 'regained' implies the town was not Saadi land continuously from 1550 (ledger 1550), and the page gives no interim holder, no month and no 1577 handover. The Saadi page, which dates the Portuguese evacuation to 1550, does not name this event. Spain's dossier (spanish-empire) carries Spain's side.

region.text: the Niger bend where Judar Pasha's army met the Songhai

ledger.note: March 1591: the Moroccans defeat the Songhai at Tondibi. 'In October 1590, he dispatched a force under Judar Pasha'; Judar reached the Niger on 28 February 1591; Tondibi is dated 13 March 1591.

region.text: the Niger bend, held by the Moroccans after Timbuktu

ledger.note: 30 May 1591: Timbuktu falls and the Niger bend becomes a Moroccan governorate. The Moroccans 'occupied Gao and captured Timbuktu on May 30'; 'a decade of sporadic fighting followed' (Tondibi page), the Songhai of Dendi keeping their freedom after a 1630 peace.

region.text: Timbuktu and Gao, 'Moroccan Governorate (1591-1621)'

ledger.note: 1591: the Pashalik of Timbuktu is founded. 'Timbuktu became the official capital of the Pashalik'; garrisons (kasbahs) at Djenné, Konna, Kabara, Timbuktu, Bamba, Bourem, Gao and Kukiya.

region.text: Djenné, 'conquered in 1592'

ledger.note: 1592: Djenné falls to the Moroccans.
1603: Ahmad al-Mansur dies of the plague (25 August) and the realm splits for 25 years between a region ruled from Marrakesh and one ruled from Fez (infobox 'Fez (1603-1627, rival capital)').

region.text: Larache, which al-Ma'mun agreed 'to cede ... to Spain'

ledger.note: 1610: the Fez line cedes Larache to Spain. Al-Ma'mun agreed 'to cede the northern port city of Larache to Spain' and landed there in November 1610; the page does not give the day of the transfer.

region.text: the Souss: 'The Sous valley, meanwhile, had come under the leadership of 'Ali Abu Hassun al-Simlali in the town of Iligh since 1614' ('the Sus, until Draa River, under the control of the Zaouia of Illigh')

ledger.note: 1614: the Souss leaves Saadi control for the Zawiya of Illigh. The Saadi page gives 1614 for Ali Abu Hassun al-Simlali's leadership of the Sous valley from Iligh; the Dila'iya page, after Moulay Zidan's accession in 1613, lists 'the Sus, until Draa River, under the control of the Zaouia of Illigh' among the regions that escaped central Saadi control. The extent is the Souss up to the Draa River (the gazetteer's Sous region minus a 110 km radius around the Draa valley, the researcher's reading); the Draa valley itself is taken in 1631 (next events). The pages give no day, and no battle: the Saadi realm was split between Marrakesh and Fez from 1603.

region.text: Mehdya, known as La Mamora: 'captured Al-Ma'mura during the reign of Mulay Zidan in August 1614'

ledger.note: August 1614: Spain takes La Mamora (Mehdya) on the Sebou estuary. 'Mehdya, known as La Mamora, was under Spanish rule between 1614 and 1681'; the Spanish 'captured Al-Ma'mura during the reign of Mulay Zidan in August 1614' and, after negotiations with him, left a garrison of 1,500 men. The page does not say that the sultan handed the town over, and does not date the negotiations. The Moroccan recapture of 1681 belongs to the morocco dossier. The town is one cell, still inside Cliopatria's Saadi shapes, which this dossier does not carve.

region.text: the Pashalik of Timbuktu, nominally Moroccan from 1618

ledger.note: 1618: direct control of the Sudan ends. Moulay Zidan 'relinquished direct control over the Sudan territories in 1618'; the infobox has 'Moroccan Vassal (1621-1826)', and the Arma governor had ruled in practice since 1612. The relation passes to Alaouite Morocco; the end is undated on the page (Tuareg tributary from 1787).
1627: the two Saadian splinter states 'in Marrakesh and Fes were finally reunified' and Marrakesh is again the only capital.

region.text: 'He went on to conquer the Dra'a Valley and then as far Sijilmasa in the Tafilalt in 1631'

ledger.note: 1631: Abu Hassun of Iligh takes the Draa valley. The Saadi page: 'He went on to conquer the Dra'a Valley and then as far Sijilmasa in the Tafilalt in 1631'. The valley's extent is the researcher's reading (a 110 km radius around 30.4 N 6.0 W; the gazetteer has no Draa region). The Souss, held from Iligh since 1614, is the previous event.

region.text: the Tafilalt: 'Mawlay al-Sharif who was declared sultan of the Tafilalt in 1631'

ledger.note: 1631: the Tafilalt leaves the Saadi realm; Mawlay al-Sharif is 'declared sultan of the Tafilalt in 1631' (Alawi page) and the morocco dossier founds the Alawi state at Sijilmasa in the same year. The pages disagree on who held Sijilmasa in 1631-1640: the Saadi page has Abu Hassun of Iligh conquer 'as far Sijilmasa in the Tafilalt in 1631', and the Alawi page has 'Abu Hassun extended his control to the Tafilalt region in 1631' with the Alawite 'expelled Abu Hassun's forces in 1640 or 1641'. The loss is entered against morocco as in morocco's found event; the Illigh claim is in the notes. The Dila'iya page lists the Tafilalt 'under the control of the Alawites' in a list placed under 1613, which this entry does not follow because the Alawi page dates the sultanate of the Tafilalt to 1631.

region.text: Meknes, Fez and Salé, taken by the Dila'iya

ledger.note: 1641: the Dila'iya take Fez, Meknes and Salé. 'By 1641 they had taken Meknes, Fez, and Salé'; 'the Saadi family was expelled and Mohammed al-Hajj was proclaimed Sultan'. The Saadi page: the Dala'iyya 'defeated a Saadian army in 1638 and captured Fez in 1641'. The rest of the Dila'iya domain and the land that went to no state are the next two entries (1641, confidence 2 and 1).

region.text: 'From 1637 onwards, the brotherhood started with the conquest of large parts of northern Morocco'; Tetouan and other northern towns, the corridor of Taza, the Middle Atlas

ledger.note: 1641: the rest of the Dila'iya domain leaves the Saadi realm. The Dila'iya page: 'From 1637 onwards, the brotherhood started with the conquest of large parts of northern Morocco'; Tetouan and other northern towns were occupied (no year), its influence reached Ksar el-Kebir and 'the corridor of Taza to the Moulouya', and its base was the Middle Atlas; 'By 1641, they had conquered Meknes, Fez and the port of Salé' (the previous entry). The extent here mirrors the domain that morocco gains from dila-iya-sultanate in June 1668 (morocco ledger 3): Tanger-Tetouan, Taza-Al Hoceima-Taounate, Fes-Boulemane, the Gharb, the Middle Atlas around Dila, and also Chaouia-Ouardigha and Grand Casablanca, which no page opened names. The year 1641 bridges the conquest of 1637-1641; the extent is the researcher's reading on both sides.

region.text: the rest of the 1640 realm outside the Marrakesh rump and the lands lost above (Tadla-Azilal, Doukkala-Abda, the Oriental, the rest of the Middle Atlas and the Tafilalt region, the Guelmim edge)

ledger.note: 1641: the rest of the realm outside Marrakesh leaves Saadi control and no page names a holder: Tadla-Azilal, Doukkala-Abda, the Oriental (the east), the remainder of the Middle Atlas and the Tafilalt region, and the southern edge (about 150,000 km2). The Saadi page says only that 'Saadian authority outside these main centers of power was greatly diminished' in the succession conflict and that Ahmad al-Abbas 'inherited a reduced state from his father in 1655'. The Dila'iya page has the zawiya in the Middle Atlas and High Atlas, so part of this land (Tadla, the Middle Atlas) may be Dila'iya; the dila-iya-sultanate dossier should settle it. Confidence 1: a bridge across a silence.

region.text: Marrakesh, the last Saadi seat, nobody's land from 1659 to the Alawi capture of July 1668

ledger.note: 1659: the Saadi dynasty ends. 'Ahmad al-Abbas was assassinated and usurped by his maternal uncle in 1658 or 1659' (Saadi page; the page does not name the uncle or say who held Marrakesh afterwards). The Alawi page has Marrakesh captured in July 1668 and does not say who held it before. The land is therefore carried as nobody's from 1659 to 1668, as the morocco dossier does when it gains Marrakesh from 'nobody' in July 1668 (morocco ledger 4); morocco is successor in identity only. The usurper is a person, not a state any page names.

wars.name: Saadi conquest of the Wattasid realm

zones.text: Fez: the siege ended 28 January 1549; Abu Hassun retook it in January 1554 and lost it in September 1554
the Tadla plain on the Oum Er-Rbia, where the 1527 treaty partitioned Morocco

wars.outcome: The Saadians took Marrakesh in 1524 (or 1525), partitioned Morocco 'roughly along the Oum Er-Rbia River' by the 1527 Treaty of Tadla, took Fez on 28 January 1549 and, after the Ottoman-backed Abu Hassun's January 1554 victory, retook it in September 1554.
wars.note: The Battle of Tadla is undated on the page.

wars.name: Saadi-Ottoman struggle over Tlemcen
wars.outcome: The Saadians conquered Tlemcen in June 1550; Ottoman forces expelled them in February 1551. At Wadi al-Laban, north of Fez, in early 1558 the result is disputed (Abun-Nasr calls it indecisive, others a Saadian victory); no border changed.

wars.name: Battle of the Three Kings (Wadi al-Makhazin)
wars.outcome: The armies met 'at Wadi al-Makhazin near Ksar al-Kebir on August 4' and the Saadians won; Abd al-Malik I died in the battle and Ahmad al-Mansur succeeded. No territory changed hands.
wars.note: The page names the battle and the Saadi victory; Portugal as the opponent is the researcher's reading and the page was not checked for Portuguese terms.

wars.name: Moroccan invasion of the Songhai Empire

zones.text: the Niger bend: Gao, Timbuktu, Djenné; Taghaza on the way

wars.outcome: Judar Pasha left Marrakesh in October 1590, reached the Niger on 28 February 1591 and won at Tondibi on 13 March 1591; Gao and Timbuktu (30 May) fell in 1591 and Djenné in 1592. The Songhai fell back on Dendi; 'a decade of sporadic fighting followed'.
wars.note: The Tondibi page gives no year for the sack of Taghaza; the Pashalik page has 1586.

wars.name: Saadi succession war (Marrakesh and Fez lines)
wars.outcome: After al-Mansur's death 'the Saadian realm was split between a region ruled from Marrakesh and a region ruled from Fes' for 25 years; reunified in 1627.
wars.note: One state, one colour; no contest event.

wars.name: Dila'iya-Saadi war
wars.outcome: The Dila'iya defeated a Saadian army in 1638 (Saadi page) and by 1641 had taken Meknes, Fez and Salé, expelling the Saadi family from Fez.

certainty.note: No treaty line is on the pages except the roughly drawn Oum Er-Rbia partition of 1527; the Saharan and Niger holdings, the Touat and Taghaza, and the 1641-1659 rump around Marrakesh are approximate.

sources.title: Saadi Sultanate
sources.note: Identity, capitals, rulers, Marrakesh 1524/25, Treaty of Tadla 1527, Agadir 1541, Fez 1549 and 1554, Tlemcen 1550-51, Three Kings 1578, Touat 1583, civil war 1603-1627, Larache 1610, 1659. Reopened in the repair pass: Sous valley under Ali Abu Hassun at Iligh since 1614, Draa valley and Sijilmasa conquered 1631, Dala'iyya take Fez 1641, Asilah evacuated by the Portuguese 1550, Ahmad al-Abbas assassinated 1658 or 1659; silent on Mamora and Taghaza 1556.

sources.title: Battle of Tondibi
sources.note: The 1590-91 campaign: the Niger reached 28 February 1591, Tondibi 13 March 1591; thin on the dates of Taghaza and on the aftermath.

sources.title: Pashalik of Timbuktu
sources.note: Governorate 1591-1621, Timbuktu 30 May 1591, Djenné 1592, Taghaza 1556-57 and 1586, Touat 1583, 1618 direct control relinquished, the Arma.

sources.title: Zawiya Dila'iya
sources.note: The Dila'iya take Fez, Meknes and Salé by 1641; Salé 1660; annexed by the Alawites 1668. Opened as Zawiya_Dila%27iya after the unencoded and other titles failed to load. Reopened in the repair pass: 1613 list (Sus until Draa under Illigh, Tafilalt under the Alawites), conquest of the north from 1637, Meknes, Fez and Salé by 1641, Tetouan undated, Ksar el-Kebir and the Taza corridor.

sources.title: Alawi dynasty
sources.note: Al-Rashid takes Fez June 1666, destroys the Dala'iyya capital June 1668 and takes Marrakesh July 1668 (the end of the Saadi succession). Reopened in the repair pass: Mawlay al-Sharif sultan of the Tafilalt 1631, Abu Hassun's forces expelled 1640 or 1641, Marrakesh July 1668; silent on who held Marrakesh 1659-1668.

sources.title: Mehdya
sources.note: La Mamora: captured by Spain in August 1614 in Mulay Zidan's reign, Spanish 1614-1681, retaken by Mulay Ismail in 1681.

sources.title: Taghaza
sources.note: Taghaza: briefly occupied by Muhammad al-Shaykh in 1556-7, again by 200 Saadian musketeers in 1586, abandoned after 1591.

sources.title: Asilah
sources.note: Asilah: Portuguese 1471, abandoned 1549, Saadians briefly regained it in 1589 and lost it to the Spanish, Moroccan 1692; silent on 1577.

notes:
Saadi Sultanate (af-02-e). (1) Cliopatria row 1556-1740 is wrong at both ends and in the middle: the dynasty began in 1510 (infobox) and ended in 1659 (page), so the 1670 and 1738 shapes (652.8 km2 in the Draa) are marked wrong and the land after 1659 belongs to Alaouite Morocco; five new keyframes cover 1510-1523 (Souss), 1524-1548 (south of the Oum Er-Rbia), 1549-1555 (all Morocco), 1591-1617 (Niger bend) and 1641-1659 (Marrakesh rump); new keyframes override the Cliopatria shapes for their years. (2) Sudan: the Pashalik page has the governorate 1591-1621 but direct control relinquished in 1618 and the Arma deposing the governor 'after 1612'; the map holds the full shape to 1617 and a vassal tint (vassal_start 1618 with the pashalik, no vassal_end because the page gives no end date; the relation ran on to Alaouite Morocco). Pages disagree on the vassal span: infobox 'Moroccan Vassal (1621-1826)'. Taghaza was also occupied in 1556-57 (Pashalik page), not drawn. (3) The Wattasid page's dates for the fall of Fez (1548, 1550) disagree with the Saadi page's 28 January 1549, which is used. (4) Tlemcen 1550-51 is an occupation of the Zayyanid kingdom; the Zayyanid dossier ends the dynasty in 1551 with an Ottoman governor. (5) New states needing dossiers: dila-iya-sultanate (Fez/Meknes/Salé 1641-1668), pashalik-of-timbuktu (1591-1833), bou-regreg-republic (Salé; the Saadi infobox lists it as a successor; years not on the pages opened), the Zawiya of Illigh (Souss to the Draa, escaped Saadi control; no years on the page). (6) Pages silent: infobox area (no comparison possible), the Mamora 1614 handover, any Saadi holding after 1641 besides the capital, who held Marrakesh in 1659-1668, the Alawi emirate of 1631 (Alawi page: recognised sultan of the Tafilalt in 1631; Saadi page: Abu Hassun went 'as far Sijilmasa in the Tafilalt in 1631' - the two pages disagree on who held it). (7) The Dila'iya page URL needed the encoded apostrophe (%27); three other forms failed to load. (8) Gazetteer names lacking: Touat, Gourara, Taghaza (radius used).

Repair pass (2026-10-19, after the review of af-02-e): (a) The 1629-1640 shape no longer holds the Souss (Iligh since 1614, Saadi page) or, from 1631, the Draa valley and the Tafilalt; ledger losses 1614 (zawiya-of-illigh), 1631 (zawiya-of-illigh; morocco), and 1641 (dila-iya-sultanate, confidence 3 and 2; nobody, confidence 1) now explain the drop from the 1640 shape to the Marrakesh rump (about 360,000 to 30,000 km2 by the gazetteer). New keyframes saadi-sultanate_1614 and _1631; the 1612, 1629 and 1640 reviews adjusted. (b) The 1659 dissolve now hands Marrakesh to nobody, as morocco ledger 4 does; the pages name no holder for 1659-1668. (c) 1582 is drawn as the 1556 shape. (d) Added Asilah 1550 and 1589, the Taghaza occupation of 1556-57 and La Mamora in August 1614. (e) Disagreements: the Tafilalt in 1631-1640 (Saadi page: Abu Hassun of Iligh conquered it; Alawi page: Mawlay al-Sharif declared sultan of it, Abu Hassun's forces expelled 1640 or 1641; Dila'iya page lists it under the Alawites from 1613); Asilah 1549 (Asilah page) against 1550 (Saadi page); the Draa valley: Dila'iya page has the Sus 'until Draa River' under Illigh in 1613, the Saadi page has Abu Hassun conquer the Draa in 1631. (f) The reviewer's Asilah handover of 1577 is on none of the pages opened (Saadi, Asilah, Mehdya) and is not entered; the reviewer's morocco non-faults are not touched. (g) Not carved: Larache (two cells, lost 1610), La Mamora (one cell) and the Asilah and Ksar es-Seghir coast are dated in the ledger but not cut out of or added to the keyframe shapes, which follow Cliopatria's coast. (h) Gazetteer names needed: Draa valley (region; a 110 km radius around 30.4 N 6.0 W is used), Zagora, Ouarzazate, Asilah, Ksar es-Seghir, Mehdya (La Mamora), Taghaza. (i) New counterpart needing a dossier: zawiya-of-illigh (Sous and Draa from 1614, Sijilmasa claimed 1631-1640; Tazeroualt). Fix fx-49 (2 Nov 2026, request R066 of window p1650-p1659): morocco is removed from identity.successors (the other three stay). The compiler hands a dissolved state's remaining cells to its successors at the end of the dissolve year, so the 695 Marrakesh cells went to the Alawis at the end of 1659, although the Alawi page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaouite_dynasty) has 'Al-Rashid secured the surrender of Fez in June 1666' and 'In July, he captured Marrakesh' (1668) and names no holder of Marrakesh in between. The dissolve event already says the land is nobody's from 1659 to July 1668 and morocco/ledger/4 gains it from nobody; the morocco dossier's predecessors still name the Saadis. The removed entry read: {"slug": "morocco", "land": {"cliopatria": "Morocco", "year": 1670, "text": "Marrakesh and the south, taken by the Alawi sultan al-Rashid in July 1668"}, "note": "Infobox: 'Succeeded by Alawi Sultanate'. Succession in identity only: the ledger passes Marrakesh to 'nobody' in 1659, and morocco gains it from 'nobody' in July 1668 (morocco ledger 4)."}
